archetype.name: Playoff Team (shooting-first)
archetype.definition: A team with a top-two offense built on elite shot-making and a top-ten defense. The record is backed by its margin, but two of the shooting numbers holding it up are the kind that drift back toward the league.

report.headline: A real turnaround, but both sides of the three-point line are flattering it
report.take:
Memphis went 25-57 last season and ranked 26th on the site. It is now 12-5 with the fourth-best Net Rtg in the league (9.1), and none of it rests on close-game luck. W vs Pt Diff sits at -1, so the margin implies 13 wins, one more than the Grizzlies actually have. Carried over a full season the differential points to 58 wins. This is a team outscoring people, not one surviving them.

The engine is the offense: ORtg 121.3, second in the league, on the best 3P % in the NBA (39.1) and the second-best eFG % and TS %. The backcourt carries it and grades A-. Cedric Coward sits second of 108 on the shooting guard tab with a team-best +10.5 On-Off. Cam Spencer is third on the same tab with a 6.1 BPM, and Ty Jerome is using 32.1% of possessions when he plays. Second chances add to it: ORB % 30.2 ranks fifth. That shooting level is far above anything in recent franchise history; the 2024-25 team that won 48 made 36.7% of its threes.

The numbers hide how much of the defense is the same coin flipped the other way. Opponents are making only 32.5% of their threes, the lowest in the league, and that alone drives a Def Rank of 9. Inside, the defense is ordinary. Opponents finish 65.8% at the rim (18th), and the defensive glass is league-average. The split by month tells the story: 106 allowed a game in October during the 6-0 start, then 114.45 in November during a 6-5 month. That month included a 128-97 home loss to Oklahoma City and a 104-95 loss in Minnesota.

The roster is also thinner than the record. Cameron Boozer, who leads the team in minutes, is out, along with Jerami Grant and GG Jackson II. That leaves Zach Edey (+15.1 On-Off) and Isaiah Stewart as the listed bigs, behind a wing group that grades F. Boozer and Grant both carry negative On-Off numbers, so the lineup math may hold up better than the injury list suggests. Even so, the guards will be asked to do even more. Expect a very good team rather than a 58-win one: likely a playoff seed, but in a division where San Antonio and Houston are right there.

strengths.title: League-best shot-making backcourt
strengths.body: Memphis leads the league in 3P % and ranks second in eFG %, and the guards are the reason: Coward, Spencer and Wells all shoot efficiently on modest usage, while Jerome takes on the heavy creation load. The skill is real. The degree is not fully sustainable; Spencer's 72.1 TS % is a number nobody holds. Expect a top-five offense rather than a 121 ORtg all year.

strengths.title: Record matches the margin
strengths.body: Point differential per game ranks fourth, and the margin implies 13 wins against the 12 they have. Nothing here needs close games to keep breaking their way. If anything the record slightly undersells the play so far.

strengths.title: Second chances on the offensive glass
strengths.body: An ORB % of 30.2 ranks fifth, well above the league's 27.3. That is a big jump from last season's 24.7. With Edey anchoring the paint it is the most repeatable part of the offense. The open question is whether it survives three power forwards being out.

concerns.title: Defense leans on opponents' misses
concerns.body: Opponents are making a league-low 32.5% from three, and that does most of the work behind a Def Rank of 9. At the rim the defense ranks 18th, and the defensive glass is league-average. Opponent three-point shooting is mostly noise, so expect the defense to slide toward the middle of the pack. November already showed it, with points allowed a game well above October's.

concerns.title: Frontcourt thinned out by injuries
concerns.body: Boozer, Grant and Jackson are all listed out. Boozer leads the team in minutes and Grant has a 61.1 TS %. Their negative On-Off numbers soften the blow, but the depth behind Edey and Stewart is gone. With a wing group graded F, the guards will be playing bigger than they are.

concerns.title: Struggles against the elite
concerns.body: The most lopsided results of the last ten came against top teams: a 128-97 home loss to Oklahoma City and a 104-95 loss in Minnesota, where the offense was held under 100. The soft schedule has been handled with ease. The good teams have shown how this team gets beaten.

trend.note: A 6-0 October gave way to a 6-5 November as the defense leaked. The last five games (4-1, +11.4 a game) show the offense still carrying the team at a top-five level.

weekAhead.headline: Two soft home-and-road games, then Minnesota and the Lakers
weekAhead.body:
The week splits cleanly. Charlotte (4-11, 28th on the site) has the league's worst offense and lets opponents make 40% of their threes, so the trip there opens with a bad defense facing the league's best shooting team. The one catch is that the Hornets lead the league in REB %, which blunts Memphis' offensive glass. The Clippers (4-11) visit with a 25th-ranked defense and the league's worst rebounding by RPG, and they have been generous to shooting guards. That is the exact position where Memphis does its damage.

The back half is the test. Minnesota has the league's top defense (104.5 DRtg) and held Memphis to 95 points just days ago. The Wolves protect the rim (Opp Rim FG % 60, second) and have an A+ wing group against Memphis' F. The Lakers (14-3) come to Memphis with the league's best eFG % and a defense that forces turnovers at the league's top rate. Their glass is soft, though: DRB % ranks 29th. Two wins are the floor, and three would be a good week.

keyMatchups.title: Shooters vs Charlotte's leaky perimeter
keyMatchups.body: Charlotte allows a league-worst 40% from three, and Memphis makes threes at the league's best rate. The Hornets' own offense ranks last, so this should be the week's cleanest win, as long as Memphis doesn't hand them extra possessions on the glass.

keyMatchups.title: Rematch with the league's best defense
keyMatchups.body: Minnesota's 104.5 DRtg is first in the league, and the Wolves already held Memphis to 95 points on November 21. Their rim protection (60% allowed) takes away Edey's finishes. Their perimeter defense is also good enough that the three-point edge narrows. This is the game that tells you whether the offense travels against the elite.

keyMatchups.title: Offensive glass vs the Lakers
keyMatchups.body: The Lakers rank 29th in DRB %, which plays straight into Memphis' fifth-ranked ORB %. The danger runs the other way: Los Angeles forces turnovers at the league's top rate, and Memphis' ball security ranks only 18th. Possessions will decide it, and so will whether Jerome can exploit a defense that gives point guards plenty.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the offense can break 110 in Minnesota with the frontcourt this thin.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation is real: a margin that matches the record, a backcourt that ranks near the top of its tabs, and an offense that was already sixth in the league two seasons ago. What will not hold is the extremes on both ends of the three-point line. The league-best 39.1% the Grizzlies are making will cool, and the league-low 32.5% opponents are making will rise. Together those should pull the Net Rtg from 9.1 down toward the 4 to 7 range. That still makes a comfortable playoff team, but not the 58-win pace the margin projects today.

The frontcourt injuries determine how far the slide goes. If Boozer and Grant return soon, the depth issue fades and 52-plus wins is realistic. If the absences drag on, the guards' heavy workload and an F-graded wing group leave the team exposed against good defenses. A 49-55 win range reflects that, with the division race against San Antonio and Houston likely going down to the final weeks.
swingFactors: Return timeline for Boozer and Grant
Whether Spencer and Coward stay this efficient

confidence.note: 17 games, shooting-driven margins and a depleted frontcourt
